questions.question: Name the four spheres of the Earth system and state what each consists of.
questions.expected_answer: Lithosphere: the rigid rocky outer layer, the crust and uppermost mantle. Hydrosphere: all water on, under and above the surface (oceans, rivers, groundwater, ice, water vapour). Atmosphere: the layer of gases around the Earth, mostly nitrogen and oxygen. Biosphere: all living organisms and the places they live.

questions.question: Describe how the water cycle involves all four spheres.
questions.expected_answer: The Sun evaporates water from the oceans and dams (hydrosphere) into the air (atmosphere); plants release water vapour by transpiration (biosphere); vapour condenses into clouds and falls as precipitation onto the land (lithosphere), where it runs off into rivers, soaks into the ground as groundwater or is taken up by organisms, and eventually returns to the sea or air.

questions.question: Explain how clearing vegetation from a hillside affects more than one sphere.
questions.expected_answer: Biosphere: plants and habitats are removed. Lithosphere: exposed soil is eroded by rain. Hydrosphere: soil washes into rivers, making them muddy and silting up dams. Atmosphere: fewer plants take in carbon dioxide by photosynthesis. One change causes a chain of effects because the spheres interact.
